fairness.title: Fairness · ALLY Command
fairness.heading: Fairness
fairness.intro: Who got their turn how often. The rate counts only the weeks somebody had signed up – breaks are not held against anyone. The comparison shows how far they sit from the alliance average.
fairness.noModules: No read access is granted for any module.
fairness.onlyWeeks: only {count, plural, one {# week} other {# weeks}}
fairness.explainSummary: How do I read this table?
fairness.explainAppearances: Weeks in which the player played or sat on the substitutes' bench.
fairness.explainSatOut: Weeks in which they had signed up but were not fielded.
fairness.explainMissed: Signed up but did not show. Triggers the ban when the week is closed.
fairness.explainPresent: Appearances out of the weeks they were available. Weeks without a sign-up do not count – a break should not be held against anyone.
fairness.explainCompare: How their share compares to the alliance average. The number behind it is the gap in percentage points.
fairness.example: 2 appearances and sitting out twice means “2 of 4” – so 50 %. The alliance average is {percent} %. The difference is <n>{diff}</n>, which is why it says “{word}”.
fairness.explainMinus: A minus does not mean somebody did anything wrong – it only shows who was left out more often. Below three available weeks there is no comparison at all: with a single week the result would inevitably be 0 % or 100 %, and the swing would mean nothing.
fairness.zugSubline: {r4} in the R4 circle · {drove} have already driven
fairness.zugFootnote: “Planned” is how often somebody was slated as train leader – “Drove” how often they actually did it. Whoever is planned often but rarely drives has been handing it over regularly.

zug.title: Zug · ALLY Command
zug.conflictHint: – you can still save; the mark stays until it is fixed. The rhythm is drive – drive – sit out; two weeks in a row are fine.

conflict.tooSoon: {name} already drove in weeks {first} and {second} – after two drives comes the break, earliest again in week {next}.

zug.counterSubline: counted up to and including week {kw} · planned future does not count
zug.advanceMessage: “{name}” moves to the back of the queue, everyone else moves up.
zug.rotationHint: The order decides who becomes train leader next. “Last drove” shows who has been waiting longest.
zug.allInRotation: Every player is already in the rotation.
zug.openHint: On {count} day(s) there is still no planned train leader – the list says “offen” there. Fill it in on the week plan and the text is right.
zug.blocksHint: They apply to every week – set them once and the list is ready to go. The text goes into the game and therefore stays exactly as you write it.

join.heading: Self-registration
join.hint: Members create their own account – with this code and their name from the roster. Those accounts may read and sign themselves off, nothing else.
join.rotateTitle: Generate a new code – the old one stops working immediately
join.disableMessage: Without a code nobody can create an account any more. Existing accounts are untouched.
join.codeHint: Put the code into the alliance announcement in the game – only members get to see it there. Anyone who leaves the alliance still knows it: generate a new one after every departure.
join.nobodyYet: Nobody has created an account yet.

backup.title: Backups · ALLY Command
backup.heading: Backups
backup.intro: A backup is created automatically whenever a week is closed. The last {keep} are kept, older ones are dropped.
backup.listHint: Every file is a complete database.
backup.noneLong: No backup yet. The first one appears when the next week is closed.
backup.peekBody: click the file name. The backup is only read – number of players, week, sign-ups, bans and the stored line-ups per week.
backup.restoreBody: Stop the server, copy the backup from the <c>backups/</c> folder over <c>prisma/dev.db</c>, start the server. The backup is a complete database – no import needed.
backup.warnBody: a backup holds the complete data including password hashes. It therefore cannot be downloaded – the files stay on the server. Restoring requires server access.
backup.readOnlyNote: Read-only view. The running database is untouched – nothing is restored here.
backup.noLineups: No line-ups are stored in this backup.

roster.title: Alliance roster · ALLY Command
roster.intro: The player roster applies to every module. Changes here affect Wüstensturm, Schluchtsturm and Zug at the same time.
roster.heading: Player roster
roster.renameHint: New name for “{name}”. History, assignments and Zug entries stay unchanged.
roster.renameHintZug: New name for “{name}”. Zug entries stay unchanged.
roster.removeWithData:
“{name}” is leaving the alliance.

The player is taken out of Desert Storm and Canyon Battlefield. Nothing is deleted: {history} history entries and {assignments} assignments stay, and the name remains visible in the Train ({zug} entries). Reactivating restores everything.
roster.removePlain: “{name}” is leaving the alliance and is taken out of Desert Storm and Canyon Battlefield. Nothing is deleted – reactivating is possible at any time.
roster.externalsHint: Alliance members outside the ALLY roster. They drive Zug and get VIP, but they do not count against the {max} roster seats and appear neither in Wüstensturm and Schluchtsturm nor in the lastwarrank comparison.
roster.toRosterTitle: Take onto the ALLY roster – from then on also in Wüstensturm and Schluchtsturm
roster.removeExternalMessage: “{name}” is removed and then sits under “Former”. The {count} Zug entries stay in full.
roster.formerHint: Departed, deliberately not deleted: they keep their name in the rotation history, past weekly plans, bans and the train plan. If someone returns, “Reactivate” brings everything back unchanged.
roster.reactivateTitle: Take back into the alliance – the history stays intact
roster.purgeMessage: “{name}” has no entries at all – no history, no assignment, no Zug day. The record will be removed for good. For everyone else this is not even possible.
roster.footnote: Sign-up, fixed seat and bans are maintained per event in the respective module – only the master data lives here. Whoever leaves the alliance is not deleted but kept as “former”.
roster.removeRowMessage:
“{name}” is leaving the alliance.

The player is taken out of Desert Storm and Canyon Battlefield: deregistered and removed from the running week.

Nothing is deleted. {history} rotation history entries, {assignments} assignments and any bans stay, and the name remains visible in the Train ({zug} entries). If they return, everything is back with one click – including the name in the rotation history.
roster.replaceOut: Out: <n>{name}</n>. The predecessor's THP value is discarded.
roster.memberChangeHint: The predecessor leaves and stays visible with their history in past weeks. The successor starts from zero.
roster.accountChangeHint: Same person, new name: the record is renamed, history and bans carry over – retroactively too.
roster.name: Name
roster.externalCheck: External – not part of the ALLY roster
roster.externalCheckHint: Selectable for Zug only. Takes up no roster seat.
roster.externalNote: Appears only in Zug – not in Wüstensturm, Schluchtsturm or the lastwarrank comparison.
roster.normalNote: The player is then available in both tactical events – signed off and without a ban.
roster.accountGoneTitle: The game profile only shows a placeholder – the account was deleted in-game. The name here is the last known one.

r2.heading: R2 status
r2.intro: Whoever forgets the shield in the game is demoted to R2 and may not take part in Wüstensturm or Schluchtsturm. This is where it is recorded – once for both events, because the rank applies to both in the game. The mark blocks nobody: anyone can still be signed up, so the sign-ups stay complete when cross-checking. Sorting out happens by hand afterwards.
r2.pickHint: Click a name to mark it, click again to undo.
r2.historyHint: By the calendar week the mark was lifted – who came off the list that week.
r2.historyEmpty: No mark has been lifted yet.
